newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NRMA sees MLC buy as bank alternative.
newsitem.headline: NRMA sees MLC buy as bank alternative.

text.p: Unlisted Australian motoring and insurance group, the National Roads and Motorists Association (NRMA), said on Thursday its purchase of the building society unit of Lend Lease Corp's MLC Ltd unit would allow NRMA to enter the banking industry.
"Importantly, this will offer our members a genuine alternative to a bank," NRMA President Nicholas Whitlam said in a statement.
"A customer-focused building society owned by one of Australia's largest mutuals will create a significant new competitor in the Australian financial services industry."

NRMA's purchase of the MLC Building Society, which would be renamed the NRMA Building Society, would allow it to build a critical mass in home lending and cash-style products in particular, Whitlam said.
NRMA and MLC did not disclose the details of the transaction.
NRMA said the MLC purchase help its current plans for a home loan offering for members funded through Australian Mortgage Securities (AMS).
MLC Building Society, which had assets of A$770 million and 80 full-time staff, would continue to be based in Melbourne and offer its products nationally, NRMA said.
MLC produced profits of about A$1.5 million in the year to June 30, 1997, NRMA said.
MLC Building Society had 32 percent of its business in New South Wales, 30 percent in Victoria, and the rest in other states and territories, NRMA said.
The MLC buy would allow NRMA to access the payments system and the Visa card, system and help NRMA's plan to offer cash management style products.
Industry sources said NRMA paid between A$50 million and A$80 million for MLC Building Society.
